summary.symptom: compressor running loaded continuously low header pressure

citations.quote: When leakage plus demand exceed what the compressor can deliver, the compressor stays loaded, header pressure falls below the cut-in pressure, and the 5.6 bar low alarm (A-UTAIR-HDR-LO) follows. The weld cells see their regulated gun air fall shortly after; gun force alarms follow, and when gun air reaches each cell's own low limit (see the weld cell manual) the supply-air interlock stops that cell. A leak is often audible as a hiss at the leak point.
A sustained fall in header pressure while the compressor runs loaded indicates demand exceeding supply, most often a distribution leak.

| Header pressure falling, compressor loaded continuously | Distribution leak (drop legs, couplings, hoses) or a new air user | Ultrasonic leak survey of the header and the ST20/ST30 drop legs with the cells stopped | Repair the leaks; confirm the header holds pressure (see Table 3-2) |

If the combined total of line leakage and weld cell demand exceeds compressor output capacity, the unit remains loaded continuously without reaching 7.3 bar. The header pressure drops below the 6.2 bar cut-in setting until it breaches the 5.6 bar low alarm limit, triggering alarm A-UTAIR-HDR-LO.
